root_cause.text: The eventpoll structure is freed immediately in ep_free() via kfree(), while another thread may still be accessing it through RCU-protected dereferences in ep_get_upwards_depth_proc(), causing a use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds an RCU head to struct eventpoll and replaces kfree(ep) with kfree_rcu(ep, rcu) in ep_free(), with the comment "ep_get_upwards_depth_proc() may still hold epi->ep under RCU". The commit message explicitly states that ep_free() can free the struct while it is still being used by another concurrent thread.

candidates.rationale: The refcount field is part of the eventpoll structure that is freed without waiting for an RCU grace period, so even with refcounting, the immediate kfree causes a use-after-free when a concurrent RCU reader dereferences the structure.
The napi_id field is part of the eventpoll structure that becomes a dangling pointer after immediate kfree, potentially accessed via RCU in busypoll code paths.

Destroying the mutex before freeing the structure is part of the cleanup sequence, but if a concurrent RCU reader holds a reference and later tries to lock the mutex, the use-after-free will manifest.
Accessing ep->user is a dereference of the soon-to-be-freed structure; if an RCU reader later tries to access ep->user, it will be a use-after-free.
Similar to free_uid, accessing ep->ws dereferences the structure before freeing, creating a window where another thread might still hold an RCU reference to the same structure.
Directly causes the use-after-free: the eventpoll structure is freed immediately while another thread may still be accessing it through RCU-protected dereferences in ep_get_upwards_depth_proc().
